content.text: The text combines a survey of medieval architecture with a Gothic mystery narrative. It discusses Armenian, Russian, Byzantine, Romanesque, and Italian churches, emphasizing plans, domes, basilicas, towers, ornament, and cultural influences. In the narrative, Gabriel leaves Doctor Louis’s house and visits the Three Black Crows inn, where two suspicious strangers are drinking. He follows them toward the woods, but they sleep there. Gabriel then reaches his own house, finds Hartog’s daughter asleep in the cottage, and later learns that one stranger was killed while attempting to break into Doctor Louis’s house. At the crime scene, Gabriel discovers blood on shrubs along the garden path, suggesting the surviving man was wounded—casting doubt on Gabriel’s theory that the strangers quarreled and one murdered the other.
